nodes.summary: For knapsack items $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ with weights $w_i$ and a capacity $W \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ of item indices is feasible when its total weight $\sum_{i \in S} w_i$ is at most $W$.
nodes.title: Feasible knapsack selection

nodes.summary: A zero-one knapsack item consists of a weight $w \in \mathbb{N}$ and a value $v \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Knapsack item

nodes.summary: For a list of $n$ knapsack items, a knapsack result consists of a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ of item indices, the chosen items, and a natural number, the reported total value.
nodes.title: Knapsack result

nodes.summary: For every list of knapsack items and every capacity $W \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S$ and $v$ be the index set and the reported value returned by the bottom-up knapsack algorithm. Then $S$ is feasible for $W$, $v$ is the total value of $S$, and every feasible set $T$ of item indices has total value at most $v$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the zero-one knapsack algorithm

nodes.summary: For every list of $n$ knapsack items and every capacity $W \in \mathbb{N}$ with $W \ge 1$, the bottom-up knapsack algorithm costs at most $3nW$ ticks.
nodes.title: Pseudo-polynomial cost bound for knapsack

nodes.summary: For every list of $n$ knapsack items and every capacity $W \in \mathbb{N}$, the bottom-up knapsack algorithm costs exactly $n(W + 1) + n$ ticks: one for each of the $n(W + 1)$ table cells it computes and one for each of the $n$ item rows it inspects during reconstruction.
nodes.title: Exact cost of the knapsack algorithm

nodes.summary: Given knapsack items $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ with weights $w_i$ and values $v_i$ and a capacity $W \in \mathbb{N}$, the algorithm fills a table $V(i, c)$ for $0 \le i \le n$ and $0 \le c \le W$ by $V(0, c) = 0$ and, for $i < n$, $V(i + 1, c) = \max(V(i, c), V(i, c - w_i) + v_i)$ if $w_i \le c$ and $V(i + 1, c) = V(i, c)$ otherwise. Starting from $c = W$, it then inspects the rows $i = n, n - 1, \dots, 1$: if…
nodes.title: Bottom-up zero-one knapsack algorithm

nodes.summary: For knapsack items $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ with values $v_i$ and a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ of item indices, the total value of $S$ is $\sum_{i \in S} v_i$.
nodes.title: Total value of a knapsack selection

nodes.summary: For knapsack items $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ with weights $w_i$ and a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ of item indices, the total weight of $S$ is $\sum_{i \in S} w_i$.
nodes.title: Total weight of a knapsack selection

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
